mechanism_narrative: A rebound in WORKPLACES mobility over the next month will spill into more weekday shopping trips and raise RETAIL_REC within four weeks, because commuting restores routine near-work purchases and lunch-time retail visits.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises for two straight weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-28-day mean by week 4, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and WORKPLACES remains depressed, people consolidate errands into fewer neighborhood trips, which should lift retail and recreation mobility within two weeks as local discretionary activity substitutes for longer commutes.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below RESIDENTIAL-adjusted baseline pressure for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline while WORKPLACES stays below baseline but RETAIL_REC fails to improve within 2 weeks, the mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp recovery in TRANSIT after a deep decline signals easing access constraints and should push RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks, because easier station access expands shopping trips and weekend circulation.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points week-on-week after being below -35
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rebounds from below -35 by at least 5 points and RETAIL_REC does not trend upward over the next 4 weeks, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent softening in PARKS and firming in RETAIL_REC indicates weather or leisure substitution away from outdoor recreation and toward indoor shopping, so a further park decline should precede higher retail-and-recreation mobility within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below its prior 2-week average by 3 points
failure_condition: If PARKS drops by at least 3 points versus its prior 2-week average and RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A continued drop in GROCERY_PHARM alongside lower TRANSIT signals fewer essential trips and weaker overall out-of-home activity, which should depress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as discretionary shopping also contracts.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT both decline for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not fall within 2 weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises while WORKPLACES falls, people spend more time near home and reduce commuting-linked discretionary trips, causing RETAIL_REC to remain lower than its recent average over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above +8 while WORKPLACES falls below -45
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL exceeds +8 and WORKPLACES is below -45 but RETAIL_REC does not stay below its last-4-week mean across the next 4 weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A one-week reversal in TRANSIT combined with improving WORKPLACES mobility indicates restrictions are easing enough to restore trip chains, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases for 2 consecutive weeks after a monthly trough
failure_condition: If TRANSIT turns up for two weeks and WORKPLACES also improves but RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over four weeks, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility stays muted while GROCERY_PHARM recovers, the pattern points to weather-driven substitution from outdoor leisure toward indoor errands, and RETAIL_REC should rise within two weeks as indoor discretionary activity strengthens.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -5 for 2 weeks while GROCERY_PHARM rises above -18
failure_condition: If PARKS stays below -5 and GROCERY_PHARM rises above -18 but RETAIL_REC does not improve within 2 weeks, reject the hypothesis.
